title: How to store silver jewellery to prevent tarnish
description: Store silver jewellery in airtight pouches with silica gel or anti-tarnish strips, away from humidity and rubber. Setups for daily wear, long-term and travel.
intro: The best way to store silver jewellery is clean, completely dry, and sealed away from air and moisture: a small zip-lock pouch with the air pressed out, kept with a silica gel sachet or an anti-tarnish strip, inside a closed box in a cool, dry cupboard. Less air means less sulphur reaching the silver, and less tarnish.

sections.heading: Why storage matters more than polishing
paragraphs: Tarnish forms when silver reacts with sulphur compounds in the air, and moisture helps that reaction along. Every hour a piece spends exposed in a humid room is an hour of slow darkening. Good storage does not stop the chemistry, but it cuts off much of what feeds it.
That means less polishing later, which also matters for plated pieces. Every polish removes a tiny amount of surface, and on gold or rhodium plated silver, that surface is thin.

sections.heading: The basic storage kit
paragraphs: You do not need an expensive jewellery box. Most of what works is cheap and easy to find.
list: Small zip-lock bags: one per piece, so items do not scratch each other.
Silica gel sachets: the small packets that come in shoe and electronics boxes absorb moisture. Keep a few in your jewellery box.
Anti-tarnish strips or anti-tarnish cloth pouches: these absorb sulphur compounds. Replace strips as the packaging suggests, often every few months.
A plain chalk stick: some people keep one in the box to absorb moisture, a simple old trick.
A box with a close-fitting lid, kept in a cupboard rather than on a dressing table.

sections.heading: Setup 1: For pieces you wear every day
paragraphs: Daily pieces need to be easy to reach, or you will just leave them on the bedside table. Keep a small lidded box or a lined tray with a lid near where you get ready, with a silica gel packet tucked in a corner.

Each evening, wipe the piece with a soft dry cloth to remove sweat and lotion, then put it in the box. Hang chains or lay them flat with the clasp closed, so they do not tangle with your pendant or earrings.

sections.heading: Setup 2: For pieces you wear occasionally
paragraphs: For silver you wear only at festivals or functions, go airtight. Clean the piece, let it dry fully for a few hours, then seal it in a zip-lock pouch with the air squeezed out. Add a small anti-tarnish strip inside if you have one. Store the pouches together in a closed box inside a cupboard.
Label pouches with a marker if you have many similar pieces. It saves you opening every bag, which lets fresh air in, every time you look for something.

sections.heading: Setup 3: Monsoon and coastal cities
paragraphs: If you live in Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata or anywhere humid, or during the monsoon wherever you are, step up the moisture control. Refresh silica gel more often. Many sachets can be dried in sunlight or a warm oven and reused, but check the packet instructions. Keep jewellery boxes on a higher shelf rather than near the floor or an outside wall, where damp tends to collect. Avoid storing silver in the bathroom at any time of year.

sections.heading: Setup 4: Travelling with silver
paragraphs: A small travel roll or a pill organiser with separate compartments keeps pieces apart. Put each chain through a drinking straw and fasten the clasp to stop knots. Carry valuable pieces in your hand luggage, not checked bags. In hotel rooms, keep jewellery in its pouch rather than loose on the counter, especially near the bathroom.

sections.heading: Things to keep away from silver
paragraphs: Some common storage materials actually speed up tarnish. Avoid rubber bands, rubber-backed mats and some foam inserts, which can release sulphur. Old felt or wool-lined boxes can do the same. Newspapers and cardboard can hold moisture and chemicals. Keep silver away from perfume bottles, hair spray and cleaning products in the same cupboard.

Also store silver separately from imitation and plated jewellery. Pieces like Varaha's [Kundan necklace sets](/women/necklaces) have their own care needs, and loose stones or metal edges can scratch softer silver. A separate pouch for each family of jewellery keeps everything in good shape. For your [925 silver pendants](/silver), one pouch each is ideal.

faq.q: Do zip-lock bags prevent silver tarnish?
faq.a: They slow it down a lot by limiting air and moisture. Press out the air and add a silica gel sachet for best results.

faq.q: Is it okay to store silver in a velvet box?
faq.a: Many velvet boxes are fine if kept dry and closed. Avoid wool felt or rubber-backed linings, which can speed tarnish.
Chalk absorbs some moisture, which can help a little. Silica gel and anti-tarnish strips are generally more effective.

faq.q: Should I store silver chains hanging or flat?
faq.a: Either works. Hanging stops tangles, but in a humid room, flat inside an airtight pouch protects better against tarnish.
